question: Is the one-time full cost-history rescan caused by invalidating all affected cache artifacts acceptable for existing users?
rationale: Tests establish the intended state transition, but only a cost-scanner owner can accept the upgrade latency and I/O tradeoff without real-world scale evidence.

options.title: Require upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the version bumps and merge after a redacted real scan demonstrates that predecessor artifacts rebuild once and subsequent scans resume incrementally.

options.title: Accept the rebuild cost
options.body: Merge with explicit acceptance that existing Codex, Claude, Vertex AI, and pi-session cost caches will be discarded and rebuilt once.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Keep the version bumps and merge after a redacted real scan demonstrates that predecessor artifacts rebuild once and subsequent scans resume incrementally.
